source_lines.32: The hypothesis $e>n$ in [[thm-separated-hecke-residues-give-seminormal-idempotents-and-bases]] cannot be dropped. Take $F=\mathbb C$, $q=-1$ (so $e=e(\mathbb C,-1)=2$, [[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]]), $n=3$ and $\lambda=(2,1)$. The two distinct standard tableaux $s=\begin{smallmatrix}1&2\\3\end{smallmatrix}$ and $t=\begin{smallmatrix}1&3\\2\end{smallmatrix}$ have contents $\operatorname{content}_s(1),\operatorname{content}_s(2),\operatorname{content}_s(3)=0,1,-1$ and $\operatorname{content}_t(1),\operatorname{content}_t(2),\operatorname{content}_t(3)=0,-1,1$, and the extended quantum-integer identity gives $[1]_{-1}=1=[-1]_{-1}$, since $[-1]_{-1}=-(-1)^{-1}[1]_{-1}=1$. Hence $$([\operatorname{content}_s(k)]_q)_{k=1,2,3}=(0,1,1)=([\operatorname{content}_t(k)]_q)_{k=1,2,3}\quad(q=-1):$$ the q-content sequences collide although $s\ne t$, so the separation conclusion of the theorem fails. The difference of the two putative separating eigenvalues at $k=2$ is $[-1]_{-1}-[1]_{-1}=0$. Thus interpolation cannot distinguish the two tableaux: a formula that excludes equal values may still define a polynomial, but it is not a separating projector for these two labels. The attempted generator formula has axial distance $\rho=2$ and $[\rho]_{-1}=0$. In fact $L_2$ has a nontrivial Jordan block on this cell, so this cell has no simultaneous JM-eigenbasis. This explicit example shows that the uniform separation hypothesis $e>n$ cannot be dropped; it does not claim that every individual cell at every parameter with $e\le n$ lacks a seminormal basis. At the boundary $e=n=2$, still over $\mathbb C$ with $q=-1$, the row and column tableaux both have tuple $(0,1)$. The global Lagrange products in the theorem are consequently $1$ for both labels, so they are not orthogonal. Thus even the proposed replacement $e\ge n$ fails for the full global-idempotent statement.

source_lines.146: 1.4 **Transport to the Hecke tower.** For each nonzero residue-content sector, [F5] gives an algebra isomorphism $\varphi_\alpha:H^\Lambda_\alpha\to R^\Lambda(\alpha)$ for the fixed admissible normalising series, homogeneous for the transported grading. Restriction of scalars along $\varphi_\alpha$ is an exact equivalence with exact inverse given by restriction along $\varphi_\alpha^{-1}$; it preserves finite-dimensional modules, projectives and internal shifts. For every zero Hecke sector, [F6] makes the corresponding KLR sector zero as well. A unital module over the zero algebra satisfies $m=1m=0m=0$, so both Grothendieck groups of either zero sector vanish. Summing the nonzero-sector isomorphisms and these zero-group identifications over finite root supports gives $K_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(H^\Lambda)\cong K_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(R^\Lambda)$ and $G_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(H^\Lambda)\cong G_0^{\mathrm{gr}}(R^\Lambda)$. These are $A$-linear since transport commutes with internal shift, and they intertwine the Cartan maps and the forgetful maps $\zeta$ with the ungraded identifications. [F1, F3, F5, F6]

source_lines.43: **Well-definedness.** Concatenation sends the two tensor-factor identities to $e(\beta,\gamma)$ and respects the relations of each block, so $r\otimes s\mapsto r\cdot(\text{image of }s)$ is a unital algebra homomorphism from $R(\beta)\otimes_kR(\gamma)$ onto the separated-block subalgebra of the corner; note that it is unital into the corner, not into all of $R(\beta+\gamma)$, and the two block images commute because separated generators commute by relations (3), (5) and (6) with $|a-b|>1$. Injectivity is read off the PBW basis of [[thm-klr-pbw-basis-theorem]]: the monomials whose permutation word lies in the parabolic subgroup $S_{|\beta|}\times S_{|\gamma|}$ (in the appropriate block positions) and whose dot exponents are arbitrary are exactly the images of the tensor products of the two PBW bases, hence are linearly independent. The image can be strictly smaller than the corner: for $\beta=\gamma=\alpha_i$ the corner is the nil-Hecke algebra $R(2\alpha_i)\cong NH_2$, while the image is $k[x_1,x_2]e(ii)$ (with $x_1,x_2$ acting blockwise), which does not contain $\tau_1$.

source_lines.157: 5.1 **The vertical terminal alternatives.** Let $\mu$ be a multipartition and $r\downarrow_Tr+1$ at $(a,b,n)$, so the two nodes are vertically adjacent. Use the following precise tests: (a) an incoming edge $t$ with $|t-r|>1$; (b) $r\nearrow_Tr+2$ or $r+1$ is in a later component than $r+2$; (c) $r-1\nearrow_Tr+1$ or $r-1$ is in a later component than $r$. Test (a) gives $s_tT\xrightarrow{t}T$ and preserves the vertical pair. In test (b), standardness and the consecutiveness of the three entries force $s_{r+1}T$ and $s_rs_{r+1}T$ to be standard: the node of $r+2$ is above and right of $r$, hence above and right of the node of $r+1$, and after the first swap the nodes of $r,r+1$ are incomparable. Thus $s_rs_{r+1}T\xrightarrow{r}s_{r+1}T\xrightarrow{r+1}T$, while $r+1,r+2$ occupy the original vertical pair in $s_rs_{r+1}T$. The different-component case uses the same two swaps without any within-component inequality. Test (c) gives the analogous $s_rs_{r-1}T\xrightarrow{r}s_{r-1}T\xrightarrow{r-1}T$, with $r-1,r$ in the original vertical pair. If none of the tests holds, labels other than the triple adjacent to $r$ cannot have an inversion between consecutive row-reading positions: any such inverse-order consecutive pair is in incomparable nodes or distinct components and is exactly an incoming edge. Reading $r-1,r-2,\ldots,1$ backwards and $r+2,r+3,\ldots,d$ forwards consequently places them in row-reading order except for the lower-row prefix before the vertical pair and the upper-row tail after it; tests (c) and (b) exclude any further excursion. More explicitly, if $L$ is the initial label at $(a,b,n)$ and $U$ the initial label at $(a+1,b,n)$, the forced belt filling is $L,\ldots,L+b-2$ in the first $b-1$ lower-row positions, $r=L+b-1$ in $(a,b,n)$, $r+1=L+b$ in $(a+1,b,n)$, and $L+b+1,\ldots,U$ in the remaining upper-row tail; all outside entries are unchanged. A positive-weight component has a removable rim $e$-hook by [F5]. For each component $c$ use the charged infinite beta set $B_c=\{\lambda_j^{(c)}+c_c-j:j\ge1\}$. This is the ordinary beta display shifted to charge $c_c$, with all sufficiently negative positions occupied and all sufficiently positive positions vacant. A removable hook is a bead move $u\mapsto u-e$ to a gap, and its charged foot residue is $u-e+1$ modulo $e$. To see the foot formula, order the beta positions before and after the move: the affected consecutive rows form the boundary strip between the starting and ending positions, and the leftmost removed box in the last affected row has charged content one more than the ending position. The inverse move wraps a hook whose foot has charged residue one more than its starting position. Let $f$ be the charged foot residue of the hook removed from $a$. In $B_b$, choose the largest occupied integer $v\equiv f-1\pmod e$; it exists by the two tail conditions, and $v+e$ is vacant by maximality. Move $v$ to $v+e$ in component $b$. Its new hook has charged foot residue $v+1=f$. Equivalently, in an uncharged display for component $b$ the runner to use is $f-c_b-1$ modulo $e$, so different component charges cannot be ignored. Both moves stay on their own runners and preserve the component cores and total rank. The earlier of $a,b$ determines the strict dominance orientation: removing boxes there and adding them later decreases every intervening prefix sum; adding boxes there reverses the inequality. In that orientation the equal-remainder hook pair is unique, since the two changed components determine both strips. Its charged foot residues agree, so the foot difference evaluates to zero at $t=1$; it is nonzero over $F(t)$ by [F2], and consequently has a finite positive valuation. Thus the single signed contribution is nonzero, giving a Jantzen edge. If $\delta_c$ is the current component weight minus its target, then $\delta_a\ge1$, $\delta_b\le-1$, and this transfer changes $\sum_c\delta_c^2$ by $-2\delta_a+2\delta_b+2\le-2$. 5.1 Injectivity and the exact resolution. The degree of $C(t)$ in $t$ is $\lambda_i+\sum_{j
e i}(-a_{ij}) eta_j$, and its leading coefficient is the nonzero scalar $\prod_{j
e i}t_{ij}^{ eta_j}$, independent of $
u$. Its coefficients are central in $A$: unequal crossings merely permute the color-labelled factors, and on equal adjacent colors the factor product is symmetric, so its divided-difference correction vanishes. Normalize the leading coefficient to $1$. Multiplication by this central monic polynomial is injective on a free $A[t]$-module by its leading term, and hence on a projective summand. Step 4.1 therefore makes $QP$, and consequently $P$, injective. With step 2.1 this proves $0	o q^sK_1\xrightarrow{P}K_0	o Be_R	o0$. In the standard homogeneous case $\deg P=2d_i\lambda_i-\sum_a b_{i
u_a}=(\alpha_i\mid2\Lambda- eta)=s$, so this is a graded resolution; the monic branch is ungraded. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 4.1, F1, algebra]
source_lines.98: 7.2 The exact sequence (c). Tensor the bimodule resolution $0\to q^sK_1\xrightarrow{P}K_0\to Be_R\to0$ of step 5.1 over $A$ with a left $A$-module $M$. It remains exact because its cokernel $Be_R$ is right $A$-projective by step 6.1, so the original sequence is split as a sequence of right $A$-modules. By their definitions in step 1.1, $K_1\otimes_A M$ is the left-append generic induction $\bar F_iM$ and $K_0\otimes_A M$ is the right-append generic induction $F_iM$, while $Be_R\otimes_A M=F_i^\Lambda M$. The map $P$ is left $R(\beta+\alpha_i)$-linear and has homogeneous degree $s=(\alpha_i\mid 2\Lambda-\beta)$, giving exactly the functorial sequence in (c) in the declared target category. On the ungraded monic-deformation branch the same sequence is interpreted without a grading shift. [F1, step 1.1, step 5.1, step 6.1]

source_lines.52: 2.1 (Crossing words reduce.) Induct on crossing length. By [F3], a nonreduced transposition word can be changed by finitely many far and braid moves into a word with an adjacent repeat; each braid correction has three fewer crossings and is handled by induction after step 1.1, and relation (4) removes the repeated pair. For a reduced word, [F3] connects it to the chosen reduced word by finitely many braid moves; their correction terms again have fewer crossings. Thus every crossing word is a sum of chosen $\tau_w$ times dot polynomials, and step 1.1 puts the dots on the right. This proves spanning without a decreasing-length claim for braid moves themselves. [step 1.1, F2, F3, induction, algebra]
